summary: Cosmetics/perfume/body-care import bill fell to USD 58M in 2024 from >USD 500M previously; local industry covers ~70% of cosmetic needs.
implication: Finished-goods imports replaced by local filling => step-change in local demand for bottles and closures since 2023-24; closures not covered by the finished-goods ban remain importable inputs.

summary: Minister Rezig at Cosmetica North Africa: Algeria has reached self-sufficiency in cosmetics; imports of some cosmetic/hygiene products stopped; remaining challenge = local raw materials.
implication: Policy now targets upstream inputs (raw materials, packaging) = tailwind for a local closure maker; check whether closure imports face licensing/'rationalisation'.

summary: Same event: minister urged producers to work with local steelmakers on laminates/steel sheet for packaging (aerosol/metal) - packaging localisation is on the official agenda.
implication: Packaging localisation is politically supported; plastic closures are an easier win than metal - possible ANDI/incentive narrative.

summary: Algeria has not fully banned cosmetics imports but 'rationalises' them to favour local production; decision divides consumers.
implication: Import friction on finished goods; need to confirm treatment of packaging components (HS 3923.50) under import programmes.

summary: Cosmetica North Africa 2026: 330+ exhibitors incl. 125 international; ~250 Algerian companies participated; packaging an exhibited category.
implication: Hundreds of local cosmetics firms, many small = fragmented demand with many references and low per-SKU volumes (MOQ-sensitive segment).

summary: Henkel Algérie now produces 4 Schwarzkopf Gliss shampoo/care references 100% in Algeria; shown at FPA 18-27 Dec 2025.
implication: New local demand for premium shampoo bottles/flip-tops; multinationals usually impose global closure specs - local supplier must meet them or be locked out.

summary: Henkel invested EUR 120M to make Réghaïa liquid-detergent plant 98% automated; +40% output, -30% losses.
implication: High-speed lines need dimensionally consistent closures (capping torque, cap feeding) - quality bar higher than for small fillers.

summary: Unilever Algérie's second cosmetics/detergent plant in Oran: 26,000 m2, DZD 1.35 bn, shampoo/toothpaste/soap, target 80% local production of formerly imported range.
implication: Large-volume shampoo filling in the West; closure sourcing (local vs global) unknown.

summary: Hayat DHC Algérie (Bouinane, Blida; 900+ staff) makes Bingo/Test detergents; 15% household-cleaning share; new ~USD 100M paper investment.
implication: Large detergent buyer in Blida; Turkish group may source closures from Turkey - check.

summary: Labonedjma (Larbaâ): 200 staff, 8,800 m2, 600+ references, 5 brands, exporting to France.
implication: 600 SKUs = high closure variety, moderate volume per SKU: classic target for a flexible small molder with colour-matching.

summary: Chinese OEM blog states Laboratoires Venus 'manufactures its own packaging'.
implication: If leaders integrate packaging in-house, it may indicate local supply was insufficient (supports gap) and reduces the addressable market at the top end.

summary: Algerian contract fillers (Dermal Group, Sabrinel, Groupe ECI, White Industry) offer OEM/private label with minimums.
implication: Contract fillers aggregate small brands' closure needs: channel partner candidates.

summary: SGT Algeria: 2.8 bn preforms; Husky HyCAP lines producing 800M caps/yr (2015); 63% share of independent preform conversion (2013). PTD (Blida) is No. 2 preform maker with a caps unit.
implication: Commodity beverage closures are well supplied at huge scale: no gap, avoid.

summary: SGT opened Sétif cap-only site: 7 injection presses, ~2 bn caps/yr, 11 HDPE cap families.
implication: Confirms 'caps in general' are not a nationwide gap; any gap must be in non-beverage, dispensing, custom or low-MOQ closures.

summary: SARL SIPEM (ZI Oued Smar, Algiers; since 1982) advertises injection of caps with handles, dispenser caps and pumps.
implication: At least one local maker claims dispensing closures => gap is not absolute; need to know its MOQ, range and whether it takes new customers.

summary: Kompass 'bouchons en plastique' Algeria lists makers across Algiers, Béjaïa, BBA, El Oued, Ghardaïa, Khenchela, Mascara, OEB, Sétif, Skikda incl. Laboratoires SPIC (Mohammadia: capsules and bottles for pharma/cosmetics), CROWN SARL (Mascara), FE Trading (BBA).
implication: Closure makers are geographically spread; at least one claims cosmetic capsules. Directory entries need phone verification.

summary: Facebook packaging traders (PAFIX, Draria) sell sprayers, gel pumps, soap pumps for cosmetics/parapharmacy.
implication: Pumps/triggers reach small brands via traders - likely imported (ASSUMPTION). Pumps/triggers are assembly-heavy multi-part products: not a first product for a 1-press startup.

summary: Ouedkniss cosmetic-packaging listings: PET 50-100 ml bottles with caps or sprays; 1 L opaque bottle with pump sold in lot of 6,000; 60/100 ml gel bottles with pouring caps; sellers advertising import of pharma/cosmetic bottles.
implication: Small brands buy bottle and closure together, in lots of a few thousand, often imported: a low-MOQ local closure offer must be paired with bottle makers/traders.

summary: Ouedkniss snippet: sterile glass bottles with caps from ~90 DZD (unit).
implication: Only DZD price seen; glass pharma vial, NOT a plastic closure price. No DZD price for flip-top/disc-top caps found.

summary: FR/AR/EN searches for 'fabricant bouchon flip top Algérie', 'سدادات بلاستيكية الجزائر' returned only Chinese/European suppliers and customs-tariff pages; no Algerian flip-top maker indexed.
implication: Weak evidence that dispensing-closure supply is thin or offline; not proof of a gap (Algerian SMEs are poorly indexed).

summary: Algerian tariff line 3923.50.92 'bouchons et couvercles en plastique' (سدادات وأغطية بلاستيكية).
implication: Use HS 3923.50 to pull import volumes/values (ITC Trade Map, ONS/DGD) to size closure imports - next step.

summary: Sagaci Research: nourishing/moisturising shampoo for dry/damaged hair is the largest segment, dominated by local brands like Venus; 'Life' most scanned laundry brand; Amir Clean in dishwashing.
implication: Local brands lead shampoo volumes -> local brand owners (not multinationals) are the realistic first customers.

summary: CREA president Kamel Moula: local cosmetics sufficient for domestic demand; push to produce raw materials locally and export.
implication: Business-association backing for upstream localisation; potential advocacy channel.

summary: Henkel sold Aïn Témouchent plant to SM2I consortium (Hamiani, Metidj); 160 jobs kept; 7 new activities incl. 2 subcontracted to Henkel.
implication: Henkel already uses local subcontractors; if one is packaging, it shows the qualification path for local suppliers.

summary: ENAD/Shymeca and others doubled disinfectant output during Covid (gel, liquid soap, bleach).
implication: Episode of closure/pump shortage risk for sanitiser bottles - typical demand spike for pumps/flip-tops.

summary: No sourced DZD or FOB price found for flip-top/disc-top caps in this pass; prior project long-list ESTIMATE 8-25 DZD/pc for flip-tops (unsourced).
implication: Price discovery is a must-do via calls to SIPEM, PAFIX, Ouedkniss sellers and Chinese FOB quotes.
